title: Staged rollback contracts + synthetic canary acceptance criteria after regional throttling incident
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Translate the Q1 regional throttling postmortem action items into concrete PRD updates that make staged rollbacks, synthetic canaries, and telemetry gates first-class acceptance criteria for any runtime or routing change. The recent outage on region-us-west2 (INC-2025-07) exposed gaps: rollout gates were too coarse, there was no automated canary that validated tail-latency impact at 95th/99th percentiles, and the rollback playbook lacked deterministic stop conditions. This PRD update focuses on three deliverables: (1) Define deterministic staged rollback contracts with SLO-triggered stop/rollback conditions; (2) Define synthetic canary scenarios and success metrics that must be green before broad rollout; (3) Codify observability ownership and dashboards that must exist and be validated as part of release acceptance. The update will be scoped to runtime routing, autoscale, and release pipelines (hosted + dedicated).
acceptance_criteria: Staged rollback contracts: For any runtime change affecting routing or model variant selection, a 3-stage rollout (canary 1%, regional ramp, global ramp) must be defined with explicit SLO thresholds; if 95th- or 99th-percentile latency or error-rate exceeds threshold for 5m in the canary stage, automated rollback triggers within 2m.

Synthetic canary harness: Implement a CI job that runs synthetic traffic (tail-latency and correctness prompts) against canary instances for every release; canary tests produce a pass/fail signal in CI and must be green before proceeding to ramp stage.

Telemetry gates: Dashboards (per-route, per-model) including latency P50/P95/P99, error-rate, token-cost delta, and KV-cache hit-rate must be auto-generated and declared green in the release checklist; ownership assigned to runtime-observability (ENG-22488).

Runbook integration: Rollback steps and escalation targets (SRE pager list, on-call runbook link) must be embedded in PRD; runbook must include isolation steps, diagnostic queries, and rollout-shepherd instructions for traffic shepherding and traffic pinning.
Test coverage: Add automated integration tests that simulate regional capacity loss and validate that staged rollback and fallback to compatible model variant works within acceptance latency bounds.

Audit & traceability: Every release that used staged rollback contracts must include a short post-release verification note with links to dashboards and Canary CI results; the PRD mandates storage of these artifacts for 90 days.
notes: Rationale: Postmortem INC-2025-07 identified three root causes: mismatch between canary traffic and production tail behavior, missing automated SLO-based rollback, and insufficient visibility into model variant fallbacks. We intentionally require tail-focused synthetic scenarios (not just P50) and enforce automated rollback time bounds to reduce manual response latency. Trade-offs: stricter canary gating increases time-to-ship and may increase CI flakiness; mitigations include parallelizing canary traffic generation and adding a 'fast-failure' path for low-risk config-only changes.
